title: Benchmark-driven optimization
summary: Optimize only what a reproducible measurement shows is slow or costly: establish a baseline, change one variable, remeasure, and keep the change only if the numbers justify it.

provenance.notes: Keeps ECC's loop but adds the stop rule: an optimization that adds complexity without a measured gain is reverted.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The operation to improve and the metric that defines better.

outputs.name: measurements
outputs.description: Baseline and after numbers with the method.

outputs.name: decision
outputs.description: Keep or revert, with the reason.

workflow.step: Define the metric, workload and environment; reproduce the baseline at least three times and record the spread.
Profile to find where time or memory goes before changing anything.
workflow.check: The target is a measured hot spot.

workflow.step: Change one thing and remeasure with the same workload.
workflow.check: Only one variable differs between runs.

workflow.step: Keep the change only if the gain exceeds the noise and correctness tests still pass; otherwise revert.
workflow.check: A claimed improvement is outside the noise band.

workflow.step: Record the numbers, the environment and what was tried and rejected.

constraints: Never trade correctness or safety checks for speed.
Do not cite estimates as measurements; label them.
Do not run benchmarks that call paid providers without authorization.

examples.title: Premature cache
examples.situation: A cache is proposed for a function that takes 2 ms of a 900 ms request.
examples.guidance: Profile first; the cache would save 0.2 percent and add invalidation risk, so reject it.

verification: Before and after use the same workload and are repeated.
Correctness tests pass after the change.

task.text: Optimize the hot path: profile the allocation and latency, then benchmark.
Review this performance change; is it slow code or a throughput claim without a benchmark?
